summary: Per-request model lock revoked mid-cutover causing traffic to route to compatibility variant
description:
Issue summary: During a staged (sequenced) rollout for Nimbus Health tenant nh-prod, a subset of per-request sessions observed model lock revocation mid-request which caused automatic routing to fall back to a compatibility variant (rw-compat-7b-v1) resulting in occasional response format regressions and billing discrepancy.

Impact: Intermittent degraded outputs for ~2% of requests from the tenant; higher token cost observed due to duplicate attempts in the edge retry path; customer reports sporadic failures in downstream QA checks. No full outage.

Observed behavior: Traffic that was explicitly pinned to rw-large-13b-v2 (tenant pin via per-request header) was sometimes routed to rw-compat-7b-v1 after the orchestrator emitted a 'lock_revoked' event for the per-request lock. This happened during a graceful cutover window when autoscaler preempted one dedicated pool node to finish draining.

Expected behavior: When a per-request model lock is present the orchestrator should honor the affinity until the session ends or an explicit unpin; graceful cutover should not silently fall back to compatibility variant for pinned requests.

Temporary workaround: We advised customer to set an explicit model selector in the request body (model_id + strict=true) and to disable the tenant-level canary slice for the short term. We also implemented an edge-side short-circuit to avoid double-retries for the tenant (see comments).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use nh-prod tenant credentials and create a per-request pinned session: X-Tenant: nh-prod, X-Per-Request-Pin: rw-large-13b-v2
2) Start a long-running streaming request and then trigger a scheduled autoscaler preempt on one dedicated GPU node in the pool
3) Observe routing decisions in edge-proxy logs and orchestrator snapshots for that session id
4) Reproduce by toggling prewarm=true and forcing a canary slice weight change from 0.05 -> 0.2 during drain window
logs: 2026-03-13T09:12:31Z edge-proxy[ingress] INFO request_id=rc-9f2fa pin=rw-large-13b-v2 -> routed to orchestrator-02
2026-03-13T09:12:33Z orchestrator[handler] WARN request_id=rc-9f2fa lock_revoked: reason=pool-drain target=node-27
2026-03-13T09:12:33Z serving-runtime INFO start_session session_id=rc-9f2fa model=rw-compat-7b-v1 tokens=24 latency=210ms
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: orchestrator preempt logic revoked per-request locks when node drain started which caused route-coordinator to select compatible variant as a resilient fallback.
Tracing: correlated orchestrator lock_revoked events with edge routing decisions; reproduced locally with synthetic tenant and forced drain sequence.
Telemetry: pin-affinity metrics show 48 lock_revoked events during the window; 90% of those align with autoscaler drain signals; 2% are unexplained (no drain).

Edge behavior: edge retry path will re-evaluate routing on certain non-2xx responses and may drop explicit per-request pin header in one retry path due to header normalization middleware (suspected header strip in ingress-to-orchestrator handoff).
Related code: route-coordinator change in PR #792 added extra compatibility selection when model lock not present; orchestrator PR #1201 changed preempt sequence ordering.
comments: Support (Aisha): Logged after customer Slack to #support. Provided immediate workaround and asked SRE to pause scheduled node preempts for nh-prod.
SRE (Liam): Reproduced with a local harness; confirmed orchestrator emits lock_revoked before drain completes. Will instrument more logging in preempt path. Assigned to Liam for hotfix investigation.
Customer (Nimbus Health - Lauren Park): We saw ~1 in 50 requests switch models which breaks our QA filters. Appreciate an ETA for fix — this affects a new release test.
Eng (Marisol Ortega): Noted that header normalization could strip X-Per-Request-Pin during the retry path. Suggest adding an assertion in the edge retry to preserve pin headers. Draft PR queued.
SRE (Liam): Added temporary feature-flag to prevent per-request lock revocation during drain for enterprise-tier tenants; rolling to us-east only. Monitoring for side effects.
root_cause_analysis: Race between orchestrator preempt sequence and the route-coordinator header evaluation: when a dedicated pool node enters drain it triggers lock_revoked events before route-coordinator has confirmed session handoff. Concurrently, edge retry middleware normalizes headers and can strip per-request pin on retry which leads the route-coordinator to consider the request unpinned and select a compatible fallback variant.
resolution: Hotfix plan: (1) adjust orchestrator preempt ordering so lock_revoked is emitted only after session handoff confirmation; (2) patch edge retry middleware to preserve X-Per-Request-Pin across retries; (3) add a temporary enterprise-only guard to skip lock revocation during scheduled drains until fix lands. Deployed guard to us-east; full fix targeted in orchestrator and route-coordinator PRs.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-13T16:40Z: enterprise guard deployed to us-east for nh-prod. Observed lock_revoked events drop to 2 during monitoring window (from 48).
2026-03-14T02:10Z: Edge middleware patch PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-middleware/pull/314 - preserves X-Per-Request-Pin header on internal retries.
Follow-up: orchestrator PR to reorder preempt sequence assigned to release 2026-03-20 (github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/1201).
follow_up_actions: QA: create a regression suite that simulates node drain + canary weight shift while exercising per-request pins
Observability: add a pin-coherence dashboard to show lock_revoked events correlated with tenant routing shifts
Product: review canary weight automation to avoid mid-drain weight changes for enterprise tenants
resolution_status: Partial mitigation applied; engineering fix scheduled
